claim: Whole-brain atlases put the greatest neuronal type diversity in brain stem, interbrain and pallidum, not cortex or cerebellum
quote: the greatest diversity of neuronal cell types resides in deep subcortical regions within the brain stem, interbrain (hypothalamus and thalamus), and pallidum

claim: Learning-centre subregions duplicate the same cell types; brainstem and hypothalamic subnuclei consist of discrete bespoke types
quote: most subnuclei in the brain stem and hypothalamus are composed of highly discrete, bespoke cell types

claim: Learning-subsystem structures are built from repetitive copies of simple units (minicolumn, spiny neuron, microcomplex)
quote: they are built from repetitive copies of simpler units, such as the cortical minicolumn, the striatal spiny neuron, or the cerebellar microcomplex

claim: Cortical content is set by inputs and training data, not cell types, explaining similar cytoarchitecture across functions
quote: is largely determined by the inputs and the training data, rather than by the constituent cell types themselves

claim: The learning subsystem follows sublinear power-law scaling: neurons grow by orders of magnitude, type repertoire stays constant
quote: the learning subsystem follows sublinear power-law scaling

claim: Learning-subsystem neuron count is analogous to the number of model weights in artificial networks
quote: This is analogous to the ‘‘number of model weights’’ in artificial neural networks.

claim: The hominin cortex doubled in size vs chimpanzees over only 6 million years, by progenitor proliferation
quote: which doubled in size, compared with chimpanzees, over only 6 million years

claim: Von Economo neurons, once considered unique, are subtle variants of a conserved cell type
quote: are actually subtle variations of a conserved cell type rather than entirely novel types

claim: Learning-subsystem advancement comes from connectomic elaboration rather than novel transcriptomic types
quote: Regional specificity and evolutionary advancement in the learning subsystem are thus also driven by connectomic elaboration, rather than the generation of entirely novel transcriptomic cell types.

claim: The steering subsystem is likened to 'business logic' in software engineering
quote: A useful analogy for understanding the role of the steering subsystem is ‘‘business logic’’ in software engineering

claim: Swallowing relies on a medullary central pattern generator sequencing dozens of head muscles
quote: relies on a medullary central pattern generator (CPG) to orchestrate precise, sequential activation of dozens of head muscles

claim: Head-eye coordination relies on single orienting neurons broadcasting to specialized medullary and pontine modules
quote: relies on single upstream orienting neurons broadcasting to distinct, specialized modules in the medulla and pons

claim: The steering subsystem follows superlinear power-law scaling: cell types rise rapidly with neuron count
quote: the steering subsystem naturally follows superlinear power-law scaling

claim: Steering redundancy serves resilience, signal-to-noise and metabolic limits, not representational capacity
quote: Redundancy may be present, but only enough to support resilience to injury, achieve a strong signal-to-noise ratio, and manage metabolic constraints, rather than increase representational capacity.

claim: New steering cell types are favoured because they let organisms anticipate contingencies without trial-and-error learning
quote: because they enable the organism and its progeny to anticipate complex sensorimotor contingencies without the risks and temporal delay of trial-and-error learning

claim: A novel adrenal cell type drives parental care in the monogamous oldfield mouse and is absent in the deer mouse, ~20,000 years diverged
quote: diverging only ∼20,000 years ago

claim: In RL terms, the steering subsystem is the organism's reward function
quote: In the framework of reinforcement learning (RL), the steering subsystem is the organism’s reward function.

claim: Human stimulation of midbrain and hypothalamus has evoked complex emotions like despair, shame, generosity and déjà vu
quote: (the midbrain and hypothalamus) document subjects experiencing profound, complex emotions

claim: The dividing line is computational, not phylogenetic; both subsystems are ancient and even Drosophila has a learning subsystem
quote: the most coherent dividing line between the two parts is computational rather than phylogenetic

claim: Higher motivations such as compassion, social bonding and curiosity are innate drives in the steering architecture
quote: motivations like compassion, social bonding, and curiosity also constitute innate drives encoded within the steering architecture

claim: Steering plasticity resembles updating business-logic variables, not gradient-descent weight updates
quote: Steering plasticity thus resembles the updating of variables in business logic

claim: Caribou migrate by day length while their food plants grow by temperature, so climate change desynchronised them
quote: caribou time their seasonal migration using day lengths, while the plants they eat time their growth based on temperature

claim: GWAS places schizophrenia/bipolar liability in learning-subsystem cells (cortical pyramidal, striatal MSNs)
quote: have consistently placed the genetic liability for disorders like schizophrenia and bipolar disorder within the cellular hardware of the learning subsystem

claim: Standard psychiatric drugs largely target steering-subsystem neuromodulatory outputs (dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine)
quote: largely targets neuromodulatory outputs of the steering subsystem

claim: Dampening learning-subsystem hardware risks broad cognitive side effects, akin to freezing a misaligned AI's weights
quote: it is akin to repairing a misaligned AI by freezing its network weights

claim: Rare steering cell populations express diverse neuropeptides and GPCRs, enabling targeted pharmacology of specific drives
quote: Rare, specialized cell populations express a vast and varied repertoire of unique neuropeptides and G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs)

claim: GLP-1 acts on receptors on hundreds of cell types in brainstem, hypothalamus and pallidum to modulate addiction
quote: GLP-1 acts on receptors found on hundreds of cell types in the brainstem, hypothalamus, and pallidum

claim: Once the steering subsystem devalues the drug, the learning subsystem extinguishes the addictive behaviour
quote: Once the steering subsystem devalues the drug, the learning subsystem begins to extinguish the addictive behavior.

claim: In Alzheimer's, hippocampal dysfunction appears once CA1 pyramidal loss exceeds ~20-30%
quote: when the abundant pyramidal neurons in the CA1 region typically exceed a loss threshold of approximately 20%–30%

claim: For a population of a few thousand neurons, a 30% loss is a few hundred cells, inside the noise floor of counting
quote: a symptomatic 30% loss might involve the disappearance of only a few hundred cells—a quantity that falls well within the noise floor of conventional counting methods

claim: Selective steering loss is robustly established only for pigmented populations (SNc dopaminergic, locus coeruleus)
quote: we have only robustly established selective loss in the steering subsystem when the cell populations are unusually distinct, such as when they are pigmented

claim: Parkinson's motor symptoms emerge after ~30% loss of pigmented SNc dopaminergic neurons
quote: with motor symptoms emerging after approximately 30% of these pigmented neurons are lost

claim: Steering cell-type count may not track phylogenetic advancement; rodents have drives primates lack
quote: Rodents possess plenty of highly specialized innate drives

claim: Limits on stable combinatorial epigenetic landscapes may cap how many discrete cell types a genome can generate
quote: may impose an upper bound on how many discrete cell types can be generated

claim: Learning updates behaviour in software within a lifetime; steering needs hardware updates (new cell types) over evolution
quote: the steering subsystem relies on hardware-level updates—the evolution of new cell types—which occur over far longer timescales

claim: RLHF imposes alignment post hoc and often lowers likelihood-based benchmark performance
quote: RLHF often reduces performance on likelihood-based and some task-specific benchmarks

claim: AI alignment may be a problem of architectural under-specification: transformers lack dedicated valuation components
quote: the alignment problem in AI may be a problem of architectural under-specification

claim: Because steering scales by diversification, study must exhaustively characterise thousands of unique cell types rather than shared circuit principles
quote: we must commit to exhaustively characterizing the highly specific control logic encoded within thousands of unique cell types
